name: Inverted Row
summary: A closed-chain bodyweight pull where you suspend yourself horizontally beneath a bar and pull your chest upward, targeting the upper back, lats, and biceps.

setup: Set a barbell securely in a rack at roughly waist height.
Position yourself underneath the bar facing up, so the bar aligns directly over your lower chest.
Grasp the bar with a shoulder-width grip and fully extend your arms.
Extend your legs forward, placing your heels on the floor, and brace your core and glutes to form a rigid plank from head to heels.
steps: Initiate the pull by retracting your shoulder blades and driving your elbows down and back.
Pull until your chest makes light contact with the bar, keeping your torso rigid.
Hold the peak contraction briefly while actively pinching your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself under control by extending your arms until you return to the full hang without sagging your hips.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you pull your chest toward the bar, and inhale as you lower yourself back to full extension.
cues: Pull your chest to the bar.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.

common_faults.fault: Sagging or piking the hips during the movement.
common_faults.correction: Squeeze your glutes and brace your abdominals to keep your body in a straight line from heels to head.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
common_faults.correction: Keep your shoulders packed down away from your ears to maintain proper upper-back engagement.

common_faults.fault: Cutting the range of motion short at the bottom or top.
common_faults.correction: Fully straighten your arms between reps and pull until your chest touches or nears the bar.

precautions: Ensure the barbell is racked so that pulling upward pulls the bar into the J-hooks rather than out of them.
